mechanism_narrative: The four-week upward trend in TRANSIT and GROCERY_PHARM mobility reflects a steady relaxation of movement constraints, which lowers the cost of discretionary trips and lifts RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT rose from -49.6 to -45.6 and GROCERY_PHARM rose from -22.4 to -18.6 between t-3w and t-0w.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is not higher than over the last 28 days when TRANSIT and GROCERY_PHARM both continue their four-week upward trend.

mechanism_narrative: A PARKS weekly mean crossing above -20 percent marks the seasonal shift to outdoor activity; this improves ambient footfall and spills over into nearby retail and recreation, raising RETAIL_REC within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS weekly mean crosses above -20 percent.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS moved from -30.1 in t-1w to -18.9 in t-0w.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than over the last 28 days when PARKS stays above -20 percent for at least two weekly means.

mechanism_narrative: The joint improvement in GROCERY_PHARM and TRANSIT signals a broad normalization of routine trips; the interaction predicts that consumers expand into retail-and-recreation categories, lifting RETAIL_REC over four weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM and TRANSIT both improve or hold above their t-1w levels.
evidence_refs: fact:Both series improved from t-3w to t-0w while RETAIL_REC also improved.
failure_condition: When GROCERY_PHARM and TRANSIT jointly improve, RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is not higher than over the last 28 days.

failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than over the last 28 days even though RESIDENTIAL stays below 12.0 percent.

mechanism_narrative: Flat WORKPLACES at -46.7 with rising RETAIL_REC indicates remote-work persistence and separate consumer caution fatigue; as households seek leisure despite no office return, RETAIL_REC rises within one week.

evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES stayed near -46.7 while TRANSIT improved to -45.6.
failure_condition: When WORKPLACES stays near -46.7 and TRANSIT rises, the next one-week RETAIL_REC mean is not higher than the prior one-week mean.

mechanism_narrative: Easing restrictions first show up in TRANSIT; once transit crosses above -46 percent, retail and recreation follow with a one-week lag, so RETAIL_REC rises next week.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT weekly mean rises above -46.0 percent.
failure_condition: If TRANSIT is above -46.0 percent in a weekly mean, the following weekly RETAIL_REC mean is lower than or equal to the current weekly RETAIL_REC mean.

mechanism_narrative: The sharp PARKS surge to -18.9 reflects unusually favorable spring weather; outdoor recreation substitutes for indoor retail-and-recreation venues, so RETAIL_REC declines over the next two weeks.

evidence_refs: fact:PARKS jumped from -30.1 in t-1w to -18.9 in t-0w.

mechanism_narrative: When TRANSIT recovery outpaces WORKPLACES recovery, it signals discretionary rather than commuting travel; this interaction predicts consumers re-engage with retail and recreation, lifting RETAIL_REC over four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT improves by more than 3 points week-on-week while WORKPLACES changes by less than 1 point.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT improved from -48.0 to -45.6 while WORKPLACES stayed at -46.7.
failure_condition: When TRANSIT rises more than WORKPLACES, RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is not higher than over the last 28 days.
